name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million example open-source dataset for training reasoning models via supervised fine-tuning (SFT). It covers math (850,000 examples), code (250,000 examples), and science (100,000 examples) domains. The dataset is the result of a systematic investigation of data generation pipeline design choices including question sourcing, mixing, filtering, deduplication, multiple answer sampling, answer filtering, and teacher model selection. Answers (reasoning traces) are generated using QwQ-32B as the teacher model. The dataset was used to train OpenThinker3-7B, achieving state-of-the-art results among open-data 7B reasoning models.

creator: OpenThoughts Team (Stanford University, University of Washington, BespokeLabs.ai, Toyota Research Institute, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, UCLA, JSC, LAION, NYU, UNC Chapel Hill, ASU, Lila Sciences, Cornell Tech, TUM, Open-Sci Collective)
citeAs: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, et al. Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv:2506.04178, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a multi-stage pipeline: (1) sourcing questions from 27 code, 21 math, and 14 science question sources including fully synthetic (LLM-generated), semi-synthetic (LLM using existing data as seeds), and non-synthetic (human-written) sources; (2) mixing top-performing question sources; (3) filtering questions using LLM-based difficulty or response-length methods; (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question (16x); (5) generating reasoning traces using QwQ-32B as the teacher model. Over 1,000 controlled ablation experiments were conducted to determine the best pipeline configuration.
rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from existing datasets and newly generated sources across math, code, and science domains. Math sources include ai2-adapt-dev/openmath-2-math, AI-MO/NuminaMath-1.5, GAIR/MathPile, math-ai/AutoMathText, and others. Code sources include StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, KodCode-V1, and others. Science sources include StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs (SCP-116K and textbooks), mteb/cqadupstack-physics, and others. Reasoning traces (answers) are generated by QwQ-32B.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were mixed from top-performing sources (top 1-2 sources per domain). For math and science, exact deduplication was applied using Normalized Indel similarity (LCS-based). For code, no deduplication was applied. Multiple answers (16x) were sampled per question from the teacher model. No answer filtering was applied in the final pipeline. Datasets were decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13) methods.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Question filtering: difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code (selecting hardest questions on 1-10 ICPC scale); response-length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science (selecting questions eliciting longest LLM responses). Deduplication: exact match deduplication for math and science using Normalized Indel similarity; no deduplication for code. Decontamination: samples with >=75% Indel similarity or shared 13-grams with evaluation benchmarks were removed. The final dataset contains 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reasoning traces (thinking tokens and answers) were generated by querying the QwQ-32B teacher model 16 times per question. No answer filtering was applied in the final pipeline. For earlier dataset versions (OpenThoughts-114K), DeepSeek-R1 was used as the teacher and answer verification (answer matching and unit tests for math/code, LLM judge) was applied. GPT-4o-mini was used for question filtering (difficulty scoring and response-length filtering). GPT-4.1-mini and GPT-4.1-nano were also used for response-length filtering.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: QwQ-32B (primary teacher model for OpenThoughts3); DeepSeek-R1 (used in earlier versions and ablations); GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano (used for question filtering); DeepSeek API (used for pipeline experiments at ~$300 per 31,600-sample dataset). Annotation of OpenThoughts3-1.2M with QwQ-32B required 22,000 H100 GPU hours on 16 1xNvidia GH200 nodes.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Over 1,000 controlled ablation experiments were conducted, each generating 31,600 data points and fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, to evaluate each pipeline step. Answer filtering experiments showed that no filtering strategy outperformed training on all samples (no filtering baseline), so answer filtering was omitted from the final pipeline. Verification (majority consensus, GPT verification, unit tests) did not improve downstream performance. Multiple answer sampling (16x per question) was found to be an effective scaling axis.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 16 reasoning traces (answers) generated per question by the teacher model (QwQ-32B) in the final pipeline.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (teacher model for answer/reasoning trace generation), DeepSeek-R1 (teacher model in ablations and earlier versions), GPT-4o-mini (question difficulty filtering, response-length filtering, question generation for some sources, answer verification in ablations), GPT-4.1-mini (response-length filtering for math and science), GPT-4.1-nano (response-length filtering), gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (OCR for Organic Chemistry PDFs), FastText classifiers (question and answer filtering), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (embedding-based filtering in ablations), Evalchemy (evaluation framework).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released as part of the OpenThoughts project with iterative versioning (BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, OpenThoughts3-1.2M). Artifacts are hosted on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M and the project website openthoughts.ai. Codebase released at https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts. No explicit deprecation policy stated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and associated models aim to democratize access to high-quality reasoning model training data by providing open-source alternatives to proprietary datasets. Safety analysis shows that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades pre-existing safety alignment of base models (e.g., OpenThinker3-7B has a harmfulness rate of 55.5% on Harmbench, up from 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct). The model was trained without explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data. Future work is recommended to incorporate safety-specific datasets.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses exclusively on math, code, and science domains and does not cover other reasoning domains. Question sources vary in quality, with a 17.2 percentage point gap between the strongest and weakest code sources. Distilled reasoning models trained on this data show generalization deficits (strong performance fluctuations on reasoning-invariant problem variations in Alice in Wonderland evaluations). The dataset may reflect biases present in the underlying question sources (competition math, competitive programming, StackExchange forums, organic chemistry textbooks).
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not include data for reinforcement learning training. Staged SFT or curriculum learning approaches were not explored. The dataset is limited to math, code, and science domains. Safety alignment is degraded in models trained on this data without additional safety-specific data. Generalization deficits persist in distilled models as shown by Alice in Wonderland evaluations. Some benchmarks (AMC23, MATH500) show saturation at the 1M scale, and HLE does not respond to scale. The interaction between question diversity and answer diversity across different domains, dataset sizes, and model scales remains an open question.
rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of language models to develop reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science. The dataset was used to train OpenThinker3-7B from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Also applicable for fine-tuning other base models (demonstrated with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Not recommended for reinforcement learning training without adaptation. Not recommended for use without additional safety alignment data in safety-critical applications.
